messages.subject: Logitstic regression in Stan
parts:
Can anyone help me with the following stan code please..I don't know why this code is not working. I am new to stan and Bayesin statistics...

Code:

data {
real y[2814];
real beta0[12];
int x[2814];
 }
parameters {
 realmu_beta0;
 realsigmasq_u0;
 }
transformed parameters{
 real sigma_u0;
sigma_u0<-sqrt(sigmasq_u0);
}
model{
mu_beta0~normal(0, 100);
sigmasq_u0~inv_gamma(0.0001, 0.0001);
for(i in 1:12)
 {
 beta0[i]~normal(mu_beta0,sigmasq_u0);
 }
for(j in 1:2814) {
 // y[j]~bernoulli_logit(beta0[x[j]]);
 y[j]~ bernoulli( inv_logit( beta0[x[j]]));
 }
 }
 

Data:

library(rstan)

y <- rep(0,2814)

for(i in 48:66) y[i]=1;

for(i in 196:204) y[i]=1;

for(i in 315:361) y[i]=1;

for(i in 1125:1133) y[i]=1;

for(i in 1336:1349) y[i]=1;

for(i in 1532:1541) y[i]=1;

for(i in 1680:1711) y[i]=1;

for(i in 1895:1909) y[i]=1;

for(i in 2102:2110) y[i]=1; for(i in 2199:2148) y[i]=1;

for(i in 2455:2479) y[i]=1;

x<- rep(0,2814)

for(i in 1:47) x[i]=1;

for(i in 48:195) x[i]=2;

for(i in 196:314) x[i]=3;

for(i in 315:1124) x[i]=4;

for(i in 1125:1335) x[i]=5;

for(i in 1336:1531) x[i]=6;

for(i in 1532:1679) x[i]=7;

for(i in 1680:1894) x[i]=8;

for(i in 1895:2101) x[i]=9;

for(i in 2101:2198) x[i]=10;

for(i in 2198:2454) x[i]=11;

for(i in 2455:2814) x[i]=12;

code <- stan(file = 'code.stan', data = c( "x","y"), iter = 300, chains = 4)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Logitstic regression in Stan
parts:
You need spaces between "real" and "mu_beta0".
And you need real<lower=0> as the data type for sigma_sq_u0.
But also note that Stan uses scale/sd to parameterize normal,
not variance.

And don't, whatever you do, use those inv_gamma() priors -- they're
horribly ill-behaved. Just a simple cauchy(0,s) where s is close
to the scale of the values you expect for sigma is much better
behaved.

So if you got to here by translating a BUGS example, I'd instead
suggest reading through the Stan manual section on regression and
working from one of those examples.

Also in R, it's rather inefficient to loop and you're better off with
replacing
